attempted_claim: Let Γ be a finite simplicial graph, A_Γ the associated right-angled Artin group, and 𝒪_Γ the Bregman–Charney–Vogtmann outer space (finite-dimensional contractible, Out(A_Γ)-action with finite stabilizers; points are marked skewed Γ-complexes). Does every finite subgroup G ≤ Out(A_Γ) fix a point of 𝒪_Γ — equivalently, is every finite G realized by isometries of some skewed Γ-complex X with marking h : X → S_Γ inducing the given outer automorphisms? Decide this in general, including finite subgroups mixing graph automorphisms of Γ with transvections/twists and finite GL-type subgroups preserving no cubical Γ-complex structure.
decisive_failure: Three concrete routes were attempted with bounded recovery test: (1) positive averaging over BCV outer space fails for lack of a CAT(0) fixed-point mechanism; (2) the smallest twist-essential order-2 candidate is realizable, refuting the naive counterexample; (3) literature inspection confirms the full-Out case is explicitly open. No original theorem, invariant, or counterexample emerged, so no auditable claim can be sustained.
